# User-Friendly Documentation Overhaul

**Status: DRAFT**

## Summary

Replace the current auto-generated TypeDoc documentation with hand-written, user-friendly markdown documentation in `docs/markdown/`. The current docs (`docs/html/`, `docs/md/`, and standalone markdown files in `docs/`) expose internal implementation details that aren't useful to users. The new documentation will be organized into 8 sections covering the library's features, usage patterns, and reference material. TypeDoc tooling will be removed entirely.

## Motivation

- **Current docs are internals-focused**: TypeDoc generates API docs from JSDoc, producing reference pages for every internal function (resolution, index-manager, dependency-manager, etc.). Users don't need to see these.
- **No user onboarding**: There's no getting started guide, no conceptual explanations, no examples.
- **Wrong audience**: The docs serve developers of the library, not users of it. We need docs that help someone go from "never used agentrack" to "productive with it" in minutes.
- **Future Docusaurus site**: Markdown files in `docs/markdown/` will later be fed into Docusaurus (or similar) to produce a proper documentation website.

## Requirements

### AC1: Remove TypeDoc tooling
- Remove `typedoc` and `typedoc-plugin-markdown` from devDependencies in `packages/library/package.json`
- Delete `packages/library/typedoc.json`
- Remove scripts from `packages/library/package.json`: `docs:html`, `docs:md`, `docs`, `docs:check`
- Verify `quality` script (`bun run typecheck && bun run lint && bun run test:coverage`) is unaffected (it does not reference docs)
- Verify `prepublishOnly` script (`bun run quality`) is unaffected
- Run `bun install` to update lockfile after removing deps

### AC2: Remove old documentation content
- Delete `docs/html/` directory (TypeDoc HTML output)
- Delete `docs/md/` directory (TypeDoc Markdown output)
- Delete `docs/introduction.md`
- Delete `docs/hierarchy.md`
- Delete `docs/commands.md`
- Delete `docs/issue-blockages.md`
- Delete `docs/user-auth.md`
- The `docs/` directory should be empty after cleanup (except for the new `markdown/` subdirectory)

### AC3: Create `docs/markdown/` with 8 documentation files
Create the following files, each written for users (not library developers). Use clear language, code examples, and practical guidance.

#### 3a. `docs/markdown/overview.md`
- Brief introduction: what agentrack is and why it exists
- Key features in bullet points: file-backed, event-sourced, git-friendly, designed for AI agents, zero infrastructure, CLI + JavaScript API
- Two ways to use it: CLI (`agt` command) and JavaScript library
- Quick 3-line example to create an issue (both CLI and JS)
- Link/mention of other doc sections for details

#### 3b. `docs/markdown/getting-started.md`
- Prerequisites: Node.js >= 20
- Installation: `npm install agentrack`
- Global CLI: `npm link` or `npx agt`
- Step-by-step first session:
  1. `agt init` — initialize tracker in a repo
  2. `agt create "My first issue"` — create an issue
  3. `agt list` — see your issues
  4. `agt view <id>` — inspect an issue
  5. `agt update <id> --status in-progress` — change status
  6. `agt history <id>` — see the event log
- JavaScript equivalent of the same workflow using `Tracker` class
- Where to go next (links to other sections)

#### 3c. `docs/markdown/authentication.md`
- Auth modes: `open` (no token needed), `read-only` (reads free, writes need token), `strict` (everything needs token)
- Default mode is `open`
- Configuration in `.agentrack/config.json`
- Token-based authentication: how it works, `AGENTACK_USER_TOKEN` environment variable
- User management: `agt users register <name>`, `agt users list`, `agt users revoke <name>`, `agt users regenerate <name>`
- JavaScript API: how to pass tokens programmatically
- Example: setting up auth for a multi-agent team

#### 3d. `docs/markdown/issue-object.md`
- Issue properties: id (10-char, time-sortable), title, description, status, assignee, parentId, tags, priority (1-5)
- Computed fields: createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt
- Status lifecycle: idea → todo → in-progress → done → closed
- Event sourcing model: issues are append-only event logs, state is computed by replay
- Example: full JSON output of `agt view <id>`
- Priority guide: 1=critical, 2=important, 3=normal, 4=low, 5=trivial

#### 3e. `docs/markdown/hierarchy-and-blockages.md`
**Hierarchy section:**
- Parent-child relationships via `--parentId`
- Status constraints: can't close parent with open children, child starting work auto-promotes parent
- Downward cascade: closing parent auto-closes done children
- Auto-promotion cap: parents auto-promote up to `in-progress` (not to done/closed)
- Example: epic with stories

**Blockages section:**
- Adding blockages: `agt blockages add <id> --by <blocker-id>`
- Bidirectional: blockedBy (what blocks me) and blocks (what I block)
- Lifecycle: added → active → resolved/deleted
- Auto-resolution: completing an issue auto-resolves its blockages
- Cycle detection: circular dependencies are prevented
- Impact score: issues that unblock the most work surface first
- Example: feature blocked by infrastructure work

#### 3f. `docs/markdown/storing-issues-in-git.md`
- The `.agentrack/` directory structure: config.json, index.json, dependencies.json, users.json, issues/*.json
- Independent git branch: issues stored on orphan branch `_agentrack` via git worktree
- Why: branch-independent issue access, no merge conflicts with code
- Commands: `agt push` (auto-commit + sync to remote), `agt pull` (sync from remote)
- Init scenarios: fresh setup (creates orphan branch) vs. joining existing (fetches remote branch)
- `.agentrack/` is in `.gitignore` on the code branch — issues live on their own branch
- Example: team workflow with push/pull

#### 3g. `docs/markdown/cli-reference.md`
Complete reference for all `agt` commands. For each command: syntax, description, flags, and at least one example.

Commands to document:
- `agt init` — initialize tracker
- `agt create <title>` — create issue (flags: --description, --assignee, --tags, --status, --priority, --parentId)
- `agt update <id>` — update issue (flags: --title, --description, --status, --assignee, --tags, --priority, --parentId)
- `agt list` — list issues (flags: --status, --assignee, --tags, --parentId)
- `agt view <id>` — view computed issue state
- `agt history <id>` — view event log
- `agt next <user>` — recommend next issue for a user
- `agt comments add <id> --content <text>` — add comment
- `agt comments update <id> --comment-id <cid> --content <text>` — update comment
- `agt comments delete <id> --comment-id <cid>` — delete comment
- `agt comments list <id>` — list comments
- `agt blockages add <id> --by <blocker-id>` — add blockage
- `agt blockages resolve <id> --by <blocker-id>` — resolve blockage
- `agt blockages delete <id> --by <blocker-id>` — delete blockage
- `agt blockages list <id>` — list blockages
- `agt users register <name>` — register user
- `agt users list` — list users
- `agt users revoke <name>` — revoke user access
- `agt users regenerate <name>` — regenerate user token
- `agt push` — sync issues to remote
- `agt pull` — sync issues from remote

All commands output JSON to stdout. Errors go to stderr with non-zero exit code.

#### 3h. `docs/markdown/javascript-reference.md`
Programmatic API reference. Only document the public exports (what `index.ts` re-exports), NOT internal modules.

**Tracker class:**
- Constructor: `new Tracker()` — resolves `.agentrack/` by walking up from cwd
- Methods (group by category):
  - Setup: `init()`
  - Issues: `create(title, options?)`, `update(id, options?)`, `list(filters?)`, `view(id)`, `history(id)`, `next(userName)`
  - Comments: `addComment(id, content)`, `updateComment(id, commentId, content)`, `deleteComment(id, commentId)`, `listComments(id)`
  - Blockages: `addBlockage(id, blockerId)`, `resolveBlockage(id, blockerId)`, `deleteBlockage(id, blockerId)`, `listBlockages(id)`
  - Users: `registerUser(name)`, `listUsers()`, `revokeUser(name)`, `regenerateToken(name)`
  - Sync: `push()`, `pull()`
- Each method: signature, parameters, return type, example

**Exported types:**
- `IssueProperties`, `ComputedIssue`, `IssueId`, `IssueStatus`
- `CreateIssueOptions`, `UpdateIssueOptions`, `ListFilters`
- `CommentEvent`, `BlockageInfo`, `UserInfo`
- `NextResult`
- `AgentrackError`

### AC4: Update project configuration
- Update `docs:check` removal from any CI/release workflow references
- Update `.gitignore`: remove `docs-html/` entry (no longer relevant), ensure `docs/html/` is not ignored (we may generate Docusaurus output there later)
- Update release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`): remove TypeDoc generation and GitHub Pages deployment steps (Docusaurus deployment will be a separate future task)

### AC5: Quality gates
- `bun run quality` passes (typecheck, lint, tests) — removing typedoc must not break anything
- `bun run build` still produces working `dist/` artifacts
- `bun install` succeeds after removing typedoc deps
- All 8 markdown files exist in `docs/markdown/` with non-trivial content (>100 lines each)
- No broken internal cross-references between doc files

## Implementation Notes

### File locations

**Cleanup targets:**
- `packages/library/typedoc.json` — delete
- `docs/html/` — delete directory
- `docs/md/` — delete directory
- `docs/introduction.md` — delete
- `docs/hierarchy.md` — delete
- `docs/commands.md` — delete
- `docs/issue-blockages.md` — delete
- `docs/user-auth.md` — delete

**New files:**
- `docs/markdown/overview.md`
- `docs/markdown/getting-started.md`
- `docs/markdown/authentication.md`
- `docs/markdown/issue-object.md`
- `docs/markdown/hierarchy-and-blockages.md`
- `docs/markdown/storing-issues-in-git.md`
- `docs/markdown/cli-reference.md`
- `docs/markdown/javascript-reference.md`

**Modified files:**
- `packages/library/package.json` — remove typedoc deps and scripts
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — remove TypeDoc/Pages steps
- `.gitignore` — remove `docs-html/` entry

### Agent assignments

- **library-developer**: Remove typedoc tooling from `packages/library/` (deps, config, scripts). Run `bun install` and verify quality gates.
- **library-release**: Remove old docs content from `docs/`. Write all 8 new markdown files. This is the main content work.
- **CTO**: Update `.github/workflows/release.yml` and `.gitignore` (these are in CTO's access domain).

library-developer and library-release tasks can run in **parallel** — they touch different directories.

### Writing guidelines

- **Audience**: Developers and AI agent operators who want to use agentrack. NOT library contributors.
- **Tone**: Clear, concise, practical. Avoid marketing language.
- **Code examples**: Always show both CLI and JavaScript API where applicable.
- **Cross-references**: Link between doc files where relevant (e.g., "See [Authentication](./authentication.md) for token setup").
- **Format**: Standard markdown. No frontmatter or Docusaurus-specific syntax yet (that will be added when we set up Docusaurus).

## Out of scope

- **Docusaurus setup**: Choosing, installing, and configuring a documentation site generator is a separate future task.
- **Documentation deployment**: GitHub Pages or other hosting will be set up with Docusaurus.
- **README.md changes**: The root README already covers quick start. We can update it to link to the new docs later.
- **Generated API docs**: We're not replacing TypeDoc with another auto-generation tool. The JavaScript reference will be hand-written, covering only the public API surface.
- **Search, versioning, i18n**: These are Docusaurus concerns for later.
- **Content for `packages/ui/`**: The UI package doesn't exist yet.

## Design decision update

This replaces DD-016 ("TypeDoc HTML for API documentation"). The new approach:
- Hand-written user guides in markdown (docs/markdown/)
- Only public API surface documented (Tracker class + exported types)
- Future Docusaurus site will serve these markdown files
- No auto-generated API docs from source code

32	## `agt init`
33	
34	Initialize the agentrack tracker in the current directory. Creates the `.agentrack/` directory on the `_agentrack` orphan branch.
35	
36	```bash
37	agt init
38	```
39	
40	**Output:**
41	
42	```json
43	{ "result": "OK", "path": "/path/to/project" }
44	```
45	
46	If already initialized:
47	
48	```json
49	{ "result": "ALREADY_INITIALIZED", "path": "/path/to/project" }
50	```
51	
52	**Notes:**
53	- Must be run inside a git repository.
54	- Idempotent -- running it again won't overwrite existing data.
55	- Handles two scenarios: creates a new orphan branch (fresh) or fetches an existing one (join). See [Storing issues in git](./storing-issues-in-git.md).
56

59	## `agt create`
60	
61	Create a new issue.
62	
63	```bash
64	agt create <title> [flags]
65	```
66	
67	**Arguments:**
68	
69	| Argument | Required | Description |
70	|----------|----------|-------------|
71	| `title` | Yes | Short title for the issue |
72	
73	**Flags:**
74	
75	| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
76	|------|------|---------|-------------|
77	| `--description` | string | `""` | Detailed description |
78	| `--assignee` | string | `null` | User assigned to the issue |
79	| `--tags` | string | `""` | Comma-separated tags |
80	| `--status` | string | `"idea"` | Initial status: `idea`, `todo`, `in-progress`, `done`, `closed` |
81	| `--priority` | number | `3` | Priority 1 (critical) to 5 (trivial) |
82	| `--parentId` | string | `null` | Parent issue ID for hierarchy |
83	| `--path` | string | auto | Custom file path for the issue (relative to tracker dir) |
84	
85	**Example:**
86	
87	```bash
88	agt create "Fix login bug" \
89	  --description "SSO login returns 500 error" \
90	  --assignee alice \
91	  --tags "bug,auth" \
92	  --status todo \
93	  --priority 2
94	```
95	
96	**Output:**
97	
98	```json
99	{ "id": "m1x2k9ab" }
100	```
101

104	## `agt update`
105	
106	Update an existing issue. At least one flag must be provided.
107	
108	```bash
109	agt update <issue-id> [flags]
110	```
111	
112	**Arguments:**
113	
114	| Argument | Required | Description |
115	|----------|----------|-------------|
116	| `issue-id` | Yes | The ID of the issue to update |
117	
118	**Flags:**
119	
120	| Flag | Type | Description |
121	|------|------|-------------|
122	| `--title` | string | New title |
123	| `--description` | string | New description |
124	| `--status` | string | New status: `idea`, `todo`, `in-progress`, `done`, `closed` |
125	| `--assignee` | string | New assignee (use `null` to clear) |
126	| `--tags` | string | New comma-separated tags (replaces existing) |
127	| `--priority` | number | New priority 1-5 |
128	| `--parentId` | string | New parent ID (use `null` to detach) |
129	
130	**Example:**
131	
132	```bash
133	agt update m1x2k9ab --status in-progress --assignee bob
134	```
135	
136	**Output:**
137	
138	```json
139	{ "result": "OK" }
140	```
141	
142	**Notes:**
143	- Updating status triggers hierarchy constraints. See [Hierarchy and blockages](./hierarchy-and-blockages.md).
144	- Setting status to `done` or `closed` auto-resolves any active blockages where this issue is the blocker.

148	## `agt list`
149	
150	List issues with optional filters. Returns items from the index (fast, doesn't read individual issue files).
151	
152	```bash
153	agt list [flags]
154	```
155	
156	**Flags:**
157	
158	| Flag | Type | Description |
159	|------|------|-------------|
160	| `--status` | string | Filter by status. Use `"open"` for all non-closed issues. |
161	| `--assignee` | string | Filter by assignee |
162	| `--tags` | string | Filter by tags (AND match -- issue must have all specified tags) |
163	| `--parentId` | string | Filter by parent ID. Use `null` for top-level issues. |
164	
165	**Example:**
166	
167	```bash
168	agt list --status open --assignee alice
169	```
170	
171	**Output:**
172	
173	```json
174	[
175	  {
176	    "id": "m1x2k9ab",
177	    "title": "Fix login bug",
178	    "status": "in-progress",
179	    "assignee": "alice",
180	    "tags": ["bug", "auth"],
181	    "parentId": null,
182	    "priority": 2
183	  }
184	]
185	```
186	
187	**Notes:**
188	- Results are sorted by priority ascending, impact score descending, then `createdAt` ascending.
189	- The `path` field is intentionally excluded. Use `view` to get full issue details.

460	## `agt blockages add`
461	
462	Block an issue by one or more other issues. Multiple blockers can be specified for atomic dependency creation.
463	
464	```bash
465	agt blockages add <blocked-id> --by <blocker-id> [<blocker-id> ...]
466	```
467	
468	**Arguments:**
469	
470	| Argument | Required | Description |
471	|----------|----------|-------------|
472	| `blocked-id` | Yes | The ID of the issue to block |
473	| `--by` | Yes | One or more blocker IDs |
474	
475	**Example:**
476	
477	```bash
478	# Single blocker
479	agt blockages add feature-x --by infra-setup
480	
481	# Multiple blockers (atomic -- all or nothing)
482	agt blockages add feature-x --by infra-setup db-migration config-update
483	```
484	
485	**Output:**
486	
487	```json
488	{ "result": "OK" }
489	```
490	
491	**Notes:**
492	- Cycle detection runs for each blocker. If any would create a cycle, the entire batch is rejected.
493	- Only active blockages participate in cycle detection.

771	## Error codes
772	
773	### Global errors
774	
775	| Code | Meaning |
776	|------|---------|
777	| `NOT_INITIALIZED` | No `.agentrack/` directory found. Run `agt init`. |
778	| `NOT_A_GIT_REPO` | Current directory is not inside a git repository. |
779	| `MIGRATION_REQUIRED` | `.agentrack/` exists but is not a git worktree. Remove it and re-run `agt init`. |
780	| `INVALID_STATE` | Invalid state for the operation (e.g., currently on the `_agentrack` branch). |
781	| `PUSH_FAILED` | `agt push` failed. Error message includes git output. |
782	| `PULL_FAILED` | `agt pull` failed. Error message includes git output. |
783	| `TOKEN_REQUIRED` | A token is required by the current auth mode but none was provided. |
784	| `INVALID_TOKEN` | The provided token doesn't match any registered user. |
785	| `DEFAULT_USER_MISSING` | Auth mode is `open` but no `defaultUser` is configured. |
786

1	# JavaScript reference
2	
3	Agentrack provides a programmatic JavaScript/TypeScript API via the `Tracker` class and a set of standalone worktree functions. This page documents every public export from the `agentrack` package.
4	
5	## Installation
6	
7	```bash
8	npm install agentrack
9	```
10	
11	```javascript
12	import { Tracker } from "agentrack";
13	```
14	
15	## Tracker class
16	
17	The `Tracker` class is the primary interface for interacting with agentrack programmatically.
18	
19	### Constructor
20	
21	```javascript
22	new Tracker(cwd?: string)
23	```
24	
25	| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
26	|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
27	| `cwd` | string | `process.cwd()` | Base directory for resolving `.agentrack/` |
28	
29	The constructor does not perform any I/O. It stores the `cwd` and resolves `.agentrack/` by walking up from that directory when methods are called.
30	
31	```javascript
32	const tracker = new Tracker(); // uses process.cwd()
33	const tracker = new Tracker("/path/to/project"); // explicit path
34	```
35	
36	### Setup
37	
38	#### `init()`
39	
40	Initialize the agentrack tracker in the resolved directory.
41	
42	```javascript
43	const result = await tracker.init();
44	```
45	
46	**Return type:** `InitResult`
47	
48	```typescript
49	type InitResult =
50	  | { result: "OK"; path: string }
51	  | { result: "ALREADY_INITIALIZED"; path: string }
52	```
53	
54	**Example:**
55	
56	```javascript
57	const { result, path } = await tracker.init();
58	if (result === "OK") {
59	  console.log("Initialized at", path);
60	}
61	```
62	
63	### Issues
64	
65	#### `create(params)`
66	
67	Create a new issue.
68	
69	```javascript
70	const { id } = await tracker.create({
71	  title: "Fix login bug",
72	  description: "SSO login returns 500 error",
73	  assignee: "alice",
74	  tags: ["bug", "auth"],
75	  status: "todo",
76	  priority: 2,
77	  parentId: null,
78	});
79	```
80	
81	**Parameters:** `CreateParams`
82	
83	| Field | Type | Default | Required | Description |
84	|-------|------|---------|----------|-------------|
85	| `title` | string | -- | Yes | Issue title |
86	| `description` | string | `""` | No | Detailed description |
87	| `assignee` | string | `null` | No | Assigned user |
88	| `tags` | string[] | `[]` | No | Tags for categorization |
89	| `status` | IssueStatus | `"idea"` | No | Initial status |
90	| `priority` | 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 | `3` | No | Urgency level |
91	| `parentId` | string \| null | `null` | No | Parent issue ID |
92	| `path` | string | auto | No | Custom file path (relative to tracker dir) |
93	| `author` | string | resolved | No | Override author |
94	
95	**Return type:** `CreateResult`
96	
97	```typescript
98	type CreateResult = { id: IssueId } | AgentrackError;
99	```
100	
101	#### `update(id, params)`
102	
103	Update an existing issue. At least one field must be provided.
104	
105	```javascript
106	await tracker.update("m1x2k9ab", {
107	  status: "in-progress",
108	  assignee: "bob",
109	});
110	```
111	
112	**Parameters:** `id: IssueId`, `params: UpdateParams`
113	
114	| Field | Type | Required | Description |
115	|-------|------|----------|-------------|
116	| `title` | string | No | New title |
117	| `description` | string | No | New description |
118	| `status` | IssueStatus | No | New status |
119	| `assignee` | string \| null | No | New assignee (`null` to clear) |
120	| `tags` | string[] | No | New tags (replaces existing) |
121	| `priority` | 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 | No | New priority |
122	| `parentId` | string \| null | No | New parent (`null` to detach) |
123	| `author` | string | No | Override author |
124	
125	**Return type:** `UpdateResult`
126	
127	```typescript
128	type UpdateResult = { result: "OK" } | AgentrackError;
129	```
130	
131	#### `list(params?)`
132	
133	List issues with optional filters. Returns items from the index (fast lookup).
134	
135	```javascript
136	const issues = await tracker.list({
137	  status: "open",
138	  assignee: "alice",
139	  tags: ["bug"],
140	});
141	```
142	
143	**Parameters:** `params?: ListParams`
144	
145	| Field | Type | Description |
146	|-------|------|-------------|
147	| `status` | IssueStatus \| `"open"` | Filter by status. `"open"` = all except closed. |
148	| `assignee` | string | Filter by assignee |
149	| `tags` | string[] | AND filter -- issue must have ALL tags |
150	| `parentId` | string \| null | Filter by parent. `null` = top-level only. |
151	
152	**Return type:** `ListResult` -- an array of `IndexEntry` objects:
153	
154	```typescript
155	interface IndexEntry {
156	  id: IssueId;
157	  title: string;
158	  status: IssueStatus;
159	  assignee: string | null;
160	  parentId: IssueId | null;
161	  tags: string[];
162	  priority: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5;
163	}
164	```
165	
166	Results are sorted by priority ascending, impact score descending, then `createdAt` ascending.
167	
168	#### `view(id)`
169	
170	View the computed state of an issue by replaying its event log.
171	
172	```javascript
173	const issue = await tracker.view("m1x2k9ab");
174	```
175	
176	**Parameters:** `id: IssueId`
177	
178	**Return type:** `ViewResult`
179	
180	```typescript
181	type ViewResult = ComputedIssue | AgentrackError;
182	
183	interface ComputedIssue {
184	  id: IssueId;
185	  title: string;
186	  description: string;
187	  status: IssueStatus;
188	  assignee: string | null;
189	  parentId: IssueId | null;
190	  tags: string[];
191	  priority: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5;
192	  createdAt: string;
193	  createdBy: string;
194	  updatedAt: string;
195	}
196	```
197	
198	#### `history(id)`
199	
200	Retrieve the raw event log for an issue.
201	
202	```javascript
203	const events = await tracker.history("m1x2k9ab");
204	```
205	
206	**Parameters:** `id: IssueId`
207	
208	**Return type:** `HistoryResult`
209	
210	```typescript
211	type HistoryResult = Event[] | AgentrackError;
212	```
213	
214	Each event has:
215	
216	```typescript
217	interface Event {
218	  timestamp: string;   // ISO 8601
219	  type: string;        // "creation", "update", "comment", etc.
220	  author: string;
221	  content?: any;       // Varies by event type
222	}
223	```
224	
225	#### `next(assignee)`
226	
227	Get the recommended next issue for a given user. Returns the highest-priority, unblocked issue assigned to that user.
228	
229	```javascript
230	const nextIssue = await tracker.next("alice");
231	```
232	
233	**Parameters:** `assignee: string`
234	
235	**Return type:** `NextResult`
236	
237	```typescript
238	type NextResult = ComputedIssue | { result: "NO_ISSUES_AVAILABLE"; message: string };
239	```
240	
241	### Comments
242	
243	#### `commentsAdd(id, params)`
244	
245	Add a comment to an issue.
246	
247	```javascript
248	const { commentId } = await tracker.commentsAdd("m1x2k9ab", {
249	  content: "Found the root cause: expired SSO certificate",
250	});
251	```
252	
253	**Parameters:** `id: IssueId`, `params: CommentAddParams`
254	
255	| Field | Type | Required | Description |
256	|-------|------|----------|-------------|
257	| `content` | string | Yes | Comment text |
258	| `author` | string | No | Override author |
259	
260	**Return type:** `CommentAddResult`
261	
262	```typescript
263	type CommentAddResult = { result: "OK"; commentId: CommentId } | AgentrackError;
264	```
265	
266	#### `commentsUpdate(id, commentId, params)`
267	
268	Edit an existing comment. Appends a `comment-update` event.
269	
270	```javascript
271	await tracker.commentsUpdate("m1x2k9ab", "c1a2b3d4", {
272	  content: "Updated: the root cause was a configuration error",
273	});
274	```
275	
276	**Parameters:** `id: IssueId`, `commentId: CommentId`, `params: CommentUpdateParams`
277	
278	| Field | Type | Required | Description |
279	|-------|------|----------|-------------|
280	| `content` | string | Yes | New comment text |
281	| `author` | string | No | Override author |
282	
283	**Return type:** `CommentUpdateResult`
284	
285	```typescript
286	type CommentUpdateResult = { result: "OK" } | AgentrackError;
287	```
288	
289	#### `commentsDelete(id, commentId, params?)`
290	
291	Delete a comment. Appends a `comment-delete` event. The comment is excluded from future list output.
292	
293	```javascript
294	await tracker.commentsDelete("m1x2k9ab", "c1a2b3d4");
295	```
296	
297	**Parameters:** `id: IssueId`, `commentId: CommentId`, `params?: CommentDeleteParams`
298	
299	| Field | Type | Required | Description |
300	|-------|------|----------|-------------|
301	| `author` | string | No | Override author |
302	
303	**Return type:** `CommentDeleteResult`
304	
305	```typescript
306	type CommentDeleteResult = { result: "OK" } | AgentrackError;
307	```
308	
309	#### `commentsList(id)`
310	
311	List all active (non-deleted) comments for an issue, with edits applied.
312	
313	```javascript
314	const comments = await tracker.commentsList("m1x2k9ab");
315	```
316	
317	**Parameters:** `id: IssueId`
318	
319	**Return type:** `CommentsListResult`
320	
321	```typescript
322	type CommentsListResult = ComputedComment[] | AgentrackError;
323	
324	interface ComputedComment {
325	  id: CommentId;
326	  author: string;
327	  content: string;
328	  timestamp: string;     // ISO 8601
329	  editedAt: string | null; // ISO 8601, or null if never edited
330	}
331	```
332	
333	### Blockages
334	
335	#### `blockagesAdd(blockedId, params)`
336	
337	Block an issue by one or more other issues. The operation is atomic -- if cycle detection fails for any blocker, no changes are written.
338	
339	```javascript
340	await tracker.blockagesAdd("feature-x", {
341	  blockerIds: ["infra-setup", "db-migration"],
342	});
343	```
344	
345	**Parameters:** `blockedId: IssueId`, `params: BlockagesAddParams`
346	
347	| Field | Type | Required | Description |
348	|-------|------|----------|-------------|
349	| `blockerIds` | IssueId[] | Yes | IDs of the blocking issues |
350	| `author` | string | No | Override author |
351	
352	**Return type:** `BlockagesAddResult`
353	
354	```typescript
355	type BlockagesAddResult = { result: "OK" } | AgentrackError;
356	```
357	
358	#### `blockagesResolve(blockedId, params)`
359	
360	Mark one or more blockages as resolved. Entries remain in the index for historical visibility.
361	
362	```javascript
363	await tracker.blockagesResolve("feature-x", {
364	  blockerIds: ["infra-setup"],
365	});
366	```
367	
368	**Parameters:** `blockedId: IssueId`, `params: BlockagesResolveParams`
369	
370	| Field | Type | Required | Description |
371	|-------|------|----------|-------------|
372	| `blockerIds` | IssueId[] | Yes | IDs of the blockers to resolve |
373	| `author` | string | No | Override author |
374	
375	**Return type:** `BlockagesResolveResult`
376	
377	```typescript
378	type BlockagesResolveResult = { result: "OK" } | AgentrackError;
379	```
380	
381	#### `blockagesDelete(blockedId, params)`
382	
383	Remove blockages entirely from the dependency index. A `blockage-deleted` event is still appended for auditability.
384	
385	```javascript
386	await tracker.blockagesDelete("feature-x", {
387	  blockerIds: ["wrong-id"],
388	});
389	```
390	
391	**Parameters:** `blockedId: IssueId`, `params: BlockagesDeleteParams`
392	
393	| Field | Type | Required | Description |
394	|-------|------|----------|-------------|
395	| `blockerIds` | IssueId[] | Yes | IDs of the blockers to delete |
396	| `author` | string | No | Override author |
397	
398	**Return type:** `BlockagesDeleteResult`
399	
400	```typescript
401	type BlockagesDeleteResult = { result: "OK" } | AgentrackError;
402	```
403	
404	#### `blockagesList(id)`
405	
406	List all blockages for an issue -- both what blocks it and what it blocks.
407	
408	```javascript
409	const info = await tracker.blockagesList("feature-x");
410	console.log(info.blockedBy); // what blocks this issue
411	console.log(info.blocks);    // what this issue blocks
412	```
413	
414	**Parameters:** `id: IssueId`
415	
416	**Return type:** `BlockagesListResult`
417	
418	```typescript
419	type BlockagesListResult = BlockageInfo | AgentrackError;

421	interface BlockageInfo {
422	  issueId: IssueId;
423	  blockedBy: Array<{ blockerId: IssueId; status: "active" | "resolved" }>;
424	  blocks: Array<{ blockedId: IssueId; status: "active" | "resolved" }>;
425	}
426	```

428	### Users
429	
430	#### `usersRegister(name)`
431	
432	Register a new user and receive a token.
433	
434	```javascript
435	const { name, token } = await tracker.usersRegister("alice");
436	console.log(`Token for ${name}: ${token}`);
437	```
438	
439	**Parameters:** `name: string`
440	
441	**Return type:** `UsersRegisterResult`
442	
443	```typescript
444	type UsersRegisterResult =
445	  | { result: "OK"; name: string; token: string }
446	  | { result: "USER_ALREADY_EXISTS"; message: string }
447	```
448	
449	#### `usersList()`
450	
451	List all registered users. Tokens are never included.
452	
453	```javascript
454	const users = await tracker.usersList();
455	```
456	
457	**Return type:** `UsersListResult`
458	
459	```typescript
460	type UsersListResult = UserInfo[];

462	interface UserInfo {
463	  name: string;
464	  registeredAt: string; // ISO 8601
465	}
466	```

469	
470	Revoke a user's token, removing their ability to authenticate.
471	
472	```javascript
473	await tracker.usersRevoke("bob");
474	```

476	**Parameters:** `name: string`
477	
478	**Return type:** `UsersRevokeResult`

480	```typescript

482	  | { result: "OK" }

486	#### `usersRegenerate(name)`
487	
488	Generate a new token for an existing user. The old token is invalidated.
489	
490	```javascript

492	```
493	
494	**Parameters:** `name: string`
495	
496	**Return type:** `UsersRegenerateResult`

498	```typescript
499	type UsersRegenerateResult =

501	  | { result: "USER_NOT_FOUND"; message: string }
502	  | { result: "INVALID_TOKEN"; message: string }
503	```
504	
505	## Worktree functions
506	
507	These standalone functions manage the git worktree where agentrack stores issue data. They are exported separately from the `Tracker` class.
508	
509	### `pushWorktree(cwd, message?)`
510	
511	Stage all changes in `.agentrack/`, auto-commit, and push to the remote `_agentrack` branch.
512	
513	```javascript
514	import { pushWorktree } from "agentrack";
515	
516	const result = await pushWorktree(process.cwd());
517	console.log(result);
518	// { synced: true, commitCount: 1 }
519	```
520	
521	**Parameters:**
522	
523	| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
524	|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
525	| `cwd` | string | required | Project directory |
526	| `message` | string | `"sync: <ISO-8601>"` | Commit message override |
527	
528	**Return type:** `WorktreeSyncResult`
529	
530	```typescript
531	interface WorktreeSyncResult {
532	  synced: boolean;
533	  commitCount?: number;
534	  message?: string;
535	}
536	```
537	
538	### `pullWorktree(cwd)`
539	
540	Pull the latest changes from the remote `_agentrack` branch.
541	
542	```javascript
543	import { pullWorktree } from "agentrack";
544	
545	const result = await pullWorktree(process.cwd());
546	console.log(result);
547	// { updated: true }
548	```
549	
550	**Parameters:** `cwd: string`
551	
552	**Return type:** `WorktreePullResult`
553	
554	```typescript
555	interface WorktreePullResult {
556	  updated: boolean;
557	}
558	```
559	
560	### `initWorktree(cwd)`
561	
562	Initialize the git worktree for agentrack. Called internally by `Tracker.init()`.
563	
564	```javascript
565	import { initWorktree } from "agentrack";
566	
567	const result = await initWorktree(process.cwd());
568	```
569	
570	**Return type:** `WorktreeInitResult`
571	
572	```typescript
573	interface WorktreeInitResult {
574	  scenario: "fresh" | "join" | "already_initialized";
575	  path: string;
576	}
577	```
578	
579	### `initFreshWorktree(cwd)`
580	
581	Initialize a new orphan branch worktree. Throws if one already exists.
582	
583	### `initJoinWorktree(cwd)`
584	
585	Join an existing `_agentrack` branch from the remote. Throws if no remote branch exists.
586	
587	### `detectInitScenario(cwd)`
588	
589	Detect whether the tracker should be initialized fresh or should join an existing remote setup.
590	
591	### `isWorktreeInitialized(cwd)`
592	
593	Check whether the agentrack worktree is already set up. Returns `true` or `false`.
594	
595	### Constants
596	
597	```javascript
598	import { WORKTREE_BRANCH, WORKTREE_DIR } from "agentrack";
599	
600	WORKTREE_BRANCH; // "_agentrack"
601	WORKTREE_DIR;    // ".agentrack"

675	  IndexEntry,

680	} from "agentrack";
681	```
682	
683	## Error handling
684	
685	All methods that can fail return an `AgentrackError` instead of throwing. Check the `result` field to detect errors:
686	
687	```javascript
688	const issue = await tracker.view("nonexistent");
689	if ("result" in issue && issue.result !== "OK") {
690	  // It's an error
691	  console.error(issue.result);   // Error code, e.g. "NOT_FOUND"
692	  console.error(issue.message);  // Human-readable message
693	} else {
694	  // It's a ComputedIssue
695	  console.log(issue.title);
696	}
697	```
698	
699	Common error codes:
700	
701	| Code | Meaning |
702	|------|---------|
703	| `NOT_FOUND` | Issue ID doesn't exist |
704	| `NOT_INITIALIZED` | Tracker not initialized |
705	| `TOKEN_REQUIRED` | Auth mode requires a token |
706	| `INVALID_TOKEN` | Token doesn't match any user |

1	# Agentrack
2	
3	Agentrack is a lightweight issue tracker designed for AI agents and developers who work in git repositories. It stores issues as JSON files on a dedicated git branch, so your tracker data lives alongside your code without generating merge conflicts.
4	
5	## Why agentrack?
6	
7	Traditional issue trackers (Jira, GitHub Issues, Linear) are built around web interfaces and human workflows. Agentrack is different:
8	
9	- **File-backed** -- All data lives in JSON files. No database, no server, no infrastructure.
10	- **Event-sourced** -- Every change is an immutable event. The current state of an issue is computed by replaying its event log, so you always have a full audit trail.
11	- **Git-friendly** -- Issues are stored on a dedicated orphan branch (`_agentrack`) via git worktree. Push and pull with standard git commands. No merge conflicts with your code.
12	- **Designed for AI agents** -- The CLI outputs JSON by default, making it easy for agents and scripts to parse. The JavaScript API gives full programmatic access.
13	- **Zero infrastructure** -- `npm install agentrack` and you're done. No accounts, no hosting, no configuration servers.
14	- **Multi-agent ready** -- Token-based authentication lets multiple agents (and humans) attribute their actions. Choose from open, read-only, or strict auth modes.
15	
16	## Key features
17	
18	### Event sourcing
19	
20	Every action on an issue -- creating it, changing its status, adding a comment, linking a dependency -- is recorded as an immutable event. The current state is always computed by replaying the event log from start to finish. This means you never lose history, and you can always understand how an issue evolved.
21	
22	### Hierarchy and dependencies
23	
24	Issues can form parent-child trees via the `parentId` property, and they can declare dependencies via blockages. The hierarchy enforces status constraints: a parent can't be closed until its children are done, and starting work on a child automatically promotes the parent. Blockages prevent work from starting until blockers are resolved. See [Hierarchy and blockages](./hierarchy-and-blockages.md).
25	
26	### Git-native storage
27	
28	Instead of a database, agentrack stores everything in JSON files on a dedicated git branch. This means your issues are versioned, distributed, and synced alongside your code -- but without merge conflicts. See [Storing issues in git](./storing-issues-in-git.md).
29	
30	### Token-based auth
31	
32	Multiple agents can register as users and attribute their actions via lightweight tokens. Three auth modes (open, read-only, strict) let you balance convenience and accountability. See [Authentication](./authentication.md).
33	
34	### Priority and impact scoring
35	
36	Issues have a priority from 1 (critical) to 5 (trivial). When listing or getting the next issue, agentrack sorts by priority, then by impact score (how many other issues depend on this one), then by age. This helps agents automatically pick the most important work. See [The issue object](./issue-object.md).
37	
38	## Two ways to use it
39	
40	Agentrack provides two interfaces for the same underlying tracker:
41	
42	1. **CLI** -- The `agt` command-line tool. Ideal for quick interactions, scripting, and agent tool use.
43	
44	   ```bash
45	   agt create "Fix login bug" --status todo --assignee "alice" --priority 2
46	   ```
47	
48	2. **JavaScript API** -- The `Tracker` class. Ideal for application integration, custom workflows, and batch operations.
49	
50	   ```javascript
51	   import { Tracker } from "agentrack";
52	
53	   const tracker = new Tracker();
54	   const { id } = await tracker.create({
55	     title: "Fix login bug",
56	     status: "todo",
57	     assignee: "alice",
58	     priority: 2,
59	   });
60	   ```
61	
62	## Quick example
63	
64	Here's a complete workflow in three steps:
65	
66	```bash
67	# 1. Initialize the tracker in your repository
68	agt init
69	
70	# 2. Create an issue
71	agt create "Set up CI pipeline" --status todo --tags "devops,infra"
72	
73	# 3. View all open issues
74	agt list --status open
75	```
76	
77	The equivalent in JavaScript:
78	
79	```javascript
80	import { Tracker } from "agentrack";
81	const tracker = new Tracker();
82	
83	await tracker.init();
84	const { id } = await tracker.create({
85	  title: "Set up CI pipeline",
86	  status: "todo",
87	  tags: ["devops", "infra"],
88	});
89	const issues = await tracker.list({ status: "open" });
90	```
91	
92	## Status lifecycle
93	
94	Issues progress through five statuses:
95	
96	```
97	idea --> todo --> in-progress --> done --> closed
98	```
99	
100	- **idea** -- A thought or proposal, not yet committed to.
101	- **todo** -- Accepted and planned, ready to be picked up.
102	- **in-progress** -- Someone is actively working on it.
103	- **done** -- Work is complete, awaiting review or verification.
104	- **closed** -- Final state. Resolved, abandoned, or no longer relevant.
105	
106	The `--status open` filter matches everything except `closed`.
107	
108	## What's next?

1	# Getting started
2	
3	This guide walks you through installing agentrack and running through a complete first session. By the end, you'll know how to create, update, and inspect issues using both the CLI and the JavaScript API.
4	
5	## Prerequisites
6	
7	- **Node.js >= 20** -- Agentrack uses modern JavaScript features and requires Node 20 or later.
8	- **Git** -- Your project must be a git repository. Agentrack stores issue data on a dedicated branch.
9	
10	## Installation
11	
12	Install agentrack as a dependency in your project:
13	
14	```bash
15	npm install agentrack
16	```
17	
18	This gives you access to the JavaScript API (`import { Tracker } from "agentrack"`) and the CLI command.
19	
20	### Using the CLI
21	
22	After installation, the `agt` command is available via:
23	
24	```bash
25	npx agt <command>
26	```
27	
28	For frequent use, link it globally:
29	
30	```bash
31	npm link
32	# Now you can use "agt" directly
33	agt <command>
34	```
35	
36	## Your first session (CLI)
37	
38	### 1. Initialize the tracker
39	
40	Run `init` in your git repository to create the `.agentrack` directory and set up the storage branch:
41	
42	```bash
43	agt init
44	```
45	
46	Output:
47	
48	```json
49	{ "result": "OK", "path": "/path/to/your/project" }
50	```
51	
52	This creates the `.agentrack/` directory (which lives on a separate git branch) with the index file, config, and user registry. See [Storing issues in git](./storing-issues-in-git.md) for details on how this works.
53	
54	### 2. Create an issue
55	
56	```bash
57	agt create "Investigate slow database queries" \
58	  --description "Users report the dashboard takes 10+ seconds to load. Start by profiling the database queries." \
59	  --status todo \
60	  --assignee "alice" \
61	  --tags "performance,backend" \
62	  --priority 2
63	```
64	
65	Output:
66	
67	```json
68	{ "id": "m1x2k9ab" }
69	```
70	
71	The issue ID is a short, time-sortable string. Save it -- you'll use it to reference the issue.
72	
73	### 3. List your issues
74	
75	```bash
76	agt list
77	```
78	
79	Output:
80	
81	```json
82	[
83	  {
84	    "id": "m1x2k9ab",
85	    "title": "Investigate slow database queries",
86	    "status": "todo",
87	    "assignee": "alice",
88	    "tags": ["performance", "backend"],
89	    "parentId": null,
90	    "priority": 2
91	  }
92	]
93	```
94	
95	You can filter by status, assignee, tags, or parent. For example, `agt list --status open --assignee alice` shows all open issues assigned to alice.
96	
97	### 4. View an issue's full details
98	
99	```bash
100	agt view m1x2k9ab
101	```
102	
103	Output:
104	
105	```json
106	{
107	  "id": "m1x2k9ab",
108	  "title": "Investigate slow database queries",
109	  "description": "Users report the dashboard takes 10+ seconds to load...",
110	  "status": "todo",
111	  "assignee": "alice",
112	  "tags": ["performance", "backend"],
113	  "parentId": null,
114	  "priority": 2,
115	  "createdAt": "2025-01-15T10:30:00.000Z",
116	  "createdBy": "anonymous",
117	  "updatedAt": "2025-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"
118	}
119	```
120	
121	### 5. Update the issue
122	
123	Move the issue to in-progress:
124	
125	```bash
126	agt update m1x2k9ab --status "in-progress"
127	```
128	
129	Output:
130	
131	```json
132	{ "result": "OK" }
133	```
134	
135	You can update any combination of fields in a single command:
136	
137	```bash
138	agt update m1x2k9ab --status "done" --description "Found and fixed the N+1 query in the dashboard endpoint."
139	```
140	
141	### 6. View the event history
142	
143	Every change is recorded as an immutable event. View the full history:
144	
145	```bash
146	agt history m1x2k9ab
147	```
148	
149	Output:
150	
151	```json
152	[
153	  { "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:30:00.000Z", "type": "creation", "author": "anonymous" },
154	  {
155	    "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:30:00.000Z",
156	    "type": "update",
157	    "author": "anonymous",
158	    "content": {
159	      "title": "Investigate slow database queries",
160	      "description": "Users report the dashboard takes 10+ seconds to load...",
161	      "status": "todo",
162	      "assignee": "alice",
163	      "tags": ["performance", "backend"],
164	      "priority": 2
165	    }
166	  },
167	  {
168	    "timestamp": "2025-01-15T11:00:00.000Z",
169	    "type": "update",
170	    "author": "anonymous",
171	    "content": { "status": "in-progress" }
172	  }
173	]
174	```
175	
176	The history is the source of truth. The `view` command computes the current state by replaying these events.
177	
178	## Your first session (JavaScript)
179	
180	The same workflow using the JavaScript API:
181	
182	```javascript
183	import { Tracker } from "agentrack";
184	
185	const tracker = new Tracker(); // resolves .agentrack/ from cwd
186	
187	// 1. Initialize
188	await tracker.init();
189	
190	// 2. Create an issue
191	const { id } = await tracker.create({
192	  title: "Investigate slow database queries",
193	  description: "Users report the dashboard takes 10+ seconds to load...",
194	  status: "todo",
195	  assignee: "alice",
196	  tags: ["performance", "backend"],
197	  priority: 2,
198	});
199	console.log("Created issue:", id);
200	
201	// 3. List issues
202	const issues = await tracker.list({ status: "open" });
203	console.log("Open issues:", issues);
204	
205	// 4. View an issue
206	const issue = await tracker.view(id);
207	console.log("Issue details:", issue);
208	
209	// 5. Update the issue
210	await tracker.update(id, { status: "in-progress" });
211	
212	// 6. View history
213	const events = await tracker.history(id);
214	console.log("Event log:", events);
215	```
216	
217	The `Tracker` constructor optionally accepts a `cwd` argument if you need to target a specific project directory:
218	
219	```javascript
220	const tracker = new Tracker("/path/to/project");
221	```
222	
223	## Where to go next
224	
225	- [Authentication](./authentication.md) -- Set up users and tokens so multiple agents can attribute their work
226	- [The issue object](./issue-object.md) -- Understand issue properties, statuses, and the event sourcing model

228	- [CLI reference](./cli-reference.md) -- Full command documentation with all flags and examples
229	- [JavaScript reference](./javascript-reference.md) -- Complete API reference for the Tracker class
